channel.title: The San Francisco Standard - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The San Francisco Standard (sfstandard.com)

item.title: The John Muir of ocean trash: One man’s crusade to pick up what the rest leave behind
item.description: Richard James has spent two decades bushwhacking through forests and kayaking remote waters to haul garbage from West Marin’s hidden alcoves.

item.title: Here are the lineups Giants manager Tony Vitello should use this season
item.description: With Luis Arráez at the top of the order and Rafael Devers batting second, San Francisco can generate more opportunities for its best hitters.

item.title: Trent Williams’ status will force the 49ers to pick a direction along the offensive line
item.description: Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch need to address different kinds of questions at left tackle, left guard, and center.

item.title: A quiet trade deadline doesn’t mask the Sharks’ reality: The outlook has changed
item.description: Kiefer Sherwood’s recent contract extension is a signal that veteran players want to join forces with Macklin Celebrini and a young core.

item.title: How a 60-person Bay Area tourist group got trapped in Dubai — and escaped amid war
item.description: A luxury vacation to the Middle East was unexpectedly cut short after the Iran war broke out.

item.title: SFUSD recommends pushing last day of school to June 10 to make up for strike
item.description: The district will vote March 24 on extending the school year to June 10 to meet state requirements and compensate educators for lost strike pay.

item.title: The 49ers bring back Eddy Piñeiro, addressing a top offseason priority
item.description: After one of the most accurate seasons in franchise history, Piñeiro reportedly agreed to a four-year deal to return to San Francisco.

item.title: OpenAI robotics head quits over military deal concerns
item.description: Caitlin Kalinowski cited concerns about OpenAI’s new Pentagon deal, warning that surveillance and lethal autonomy lacked sufficient guardrails.

item.title: Eileen Gu returns from Olympic fame and controversy to kick off SF Chinatown parade
item.description: Massive crowds packed downtown and Chinatown for the sold-out Lunar New Year event celebrating the Year of the Fire Horse.

item.title: Iranian-Americans cheer US military strikes
item.description: As hundreds rallied against the war in Iran, a smaller group showed up to challenge them — and celebrated possible regime change.
